0.0.n: A railway company name, used here for its rail line.

0.1.n: Marks Odakyu as the railway connected to.

0.2.n: Combines with できる to express that a rail connection is possible.

0.3.n: From できる, expressing ability; できたり lists connecting as one possibility.

0.4.n: Part of the たり…たりする pattern, which lists examples rather than every possibility.

0.6.n: Adds another item to the explanation in a conversational way.

0.7.n: A railway line name; 線 means line.

0.8.n: Marks the Keio Line as another railway connected to.

0.9.n: Combines with できる again to describe another possible rail connection.

0.10.n: From できる, expressing ability; できたり introduces another possible connection.

0.11.n: Lists the second example in the たり…たりする pattern.

0.12.n: Completes the たり list; it does not describe a separate action here.

0.13.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before です.

0.14.n: Makes the explanatory ending んです polite.

0.15.n: Highlights information the speaker is sharing with the listener.

1.0.n: Connects this conclusion to the rail connections just mentioned.

1.1.n: Strengthens 便利, suggesting a fairly high degree of convenience.

1.2.n: Describes the location as useful for getting around.

1.3.n: The linking form of だ joins the description 便利 to the next clause.

1.5.n: A place name for a major district and station area in Tokyo.

1.6.n: Presents Shinjuku as an example rather than the only destination.

1.7.n: Adds Shinjuku and similar destinations to the travel possibilities already discussed.

1.8.n: Refers to the location the speaker is discussing.

1.9.n: Marks ここ as the starting point for travel.

1.10.n: From 行ける, the ability form of 行く; 行けたり presents going there as one possibility.

1.11.n: Even a single たり can present an action as one example of what is possible.

1.12.n: Polite form of する, completing the example-listing pattern たりします.

0.lit: To Odakyu can connect, and also to Keio Line can connect, among other possibilities, you know.
0.tip: できたり…できたりする lists examples of possible connections, rather than giving an exhaustive list.

1.lit: So quite convenient, and to places like Shinjuku also, from here can go, among other possibilities.
1.tip: 行ける means can go, while たり presents that trip as one example of what you can do.
